title: AutoCheck: Automatically Identifying Variables for Checkpointing by Data Dependency Analysis
problem: System engineers and domain scientists lack automated tools to identify which critical variables must be checkpointed for correct application execution restoration during failures in Checkpoint/Restart systems. Current approaches require manual identification without systematic support for users lacking specialized fault tolerance knowledge.
motivation: Checkpoint/Restart is widely deployed in HPC systems, clouds, and industrial data centers, making automatic identification of critical checkpointing variables essential for reliable fault recovery.
method: AutoCheck analytically tracks and optimizes data dependencies between variables and application execution state, constructing a refined data dependency graph (DDG). It applies domain-agnostic heuristics to identify critical variables from the DDG for checkpointing. Programmers can identify variables within minutes, evaluated on 14 representative HPC benchmarks.
key_novelty: Automated identification of critical checkpointing variables through systematic data dependency analysis and heuristics, eliminating manual expertise requirements.
contributions: Analytical model for automatically identifying critical variables required for checkpoint/restart
AutoCheck tool implementing data dependency analysis with heuristics for efficient variable identification
Evaluation on 14 HPC benchmarks demonstrating correct identification of critical checkpointing variables

metrics.accuracy: correct identification of critical checkpointing variables (not quantified in abstract)

primary_theme: automated critical variable identification for checkpoint/restart via data dependency analysis
